goal: The ten largest economies by GDP racing across a century — a decade per second, the ranks trading places, the source on screen.
audience: anyone who likes seeing a century move
assumptions: 'a decade per second' fixes the pace: 100 years in ~10 seconds of racing plus the framing beats
the GDP figures are factual claims: each needs a source with a snapshot and a quote (open data: the World Bank / Maddison-style public datasets)
the source is credited on screen (the mission asks for it)
the covered time span is a stated assumption (a century: 1900s to 2010s/2020s)
the GDP measure is a stated assumption (nominal vs PPP — one, named)
the data's license and attribution are recorded (open data, credited on screen)
the GDP figures are sourced facts: every on-screen number carries a source snapshot + quote
the plan states its assumption (no format was named: 16:9)

decision.why: An animated chart is code-drawn motion over data: the figures land as a facts ledger (each year's ranking sourced), the bars race on the studio's springs, and the source credit sits on screen. The chart-specific capability (a data-file technique with chart gates) would fit too — motion with a data file is the smallest sufficient pipeline today.

alternatives.rejected_because: a dedicated chart technique (chart.json + data/axis gates) is the honest fit for a series of chart films; for ONE piece, motion + a data file + facts carries it without the growth step — noted in needs_capability if the studio expects more chart work

alternatives.id: simplest: a static table of the ten economies
alternatives.rejected_because: the simplest thing that could work — but 'a decade per second' IS the ask: the motion is the meaning

segments.brief: Ten bars racing rank-by-rank, a decade per second, the lead changes called out, the source credit on screen throughout. The data: each decade's top-ten GDP ranking, every figure a sourced facts entry.
acceptance: every GDP figure on screen has a facts entry (snapshot + quote)
the pace is a decade per second
the source is credited on screen
the chart shows the ten largest economies (the count is ten bars)
the chart is animated: the ranking changes over time
the pacing is a decade per second
the data is fetched and stored in the project (a data file + the facts ledger)
every on-screen number and ranking has a source_url + snapshot + quote

assembly.audio: a synthesized bed whose tempo matches a decade-per-second

needs_capability: a chart technique (chart.json data file + data/axis gates) if the studio expects a series of chart films — motion carries this one piece

risks: the dataset must be open-licensed and per-decade complete — a gap decade is hedged on screen, never invented
